name: Smart Speaker
description: The entry point for most smart homes. A smart speaker lets you control other devices, play music, set timers, and get answers hands-free using just your voice.
beginnerTip: Start here. Once you have a smart speaker, adding compatible devices becomes much simpler.

name: Smart Light Bulb
description: Swap any standard bulb for a smart bulb and control brightness, color, and on/off schedules from your phone or by voice — no rewiring required.
beginnerTip: No electrician needed. If you can screw in a lightbulb, you can install a smart one.

name: Smart Thermostat
description: Learns your schedule and preferences to heat or cool your home efficiently. Can reduce energy bills by 10–15% annually. Requires basic wiring compatibility check before purchase.
beginnerTip: Check your existing wiring with the manufacturer's compatibility tool before buying.

name: Smart Lock
description: Lock and unlock your door remotely, grant temporary access codes to guests, and get alerts when someone arrives. Most fit over your existing deadbolt hardware.
beginnerTip: Look for models that keep your existing exterior hardware so you don't need to re-key.

name: Video Doorbell
description: See, hear, and speak with visitors from your phone, even when you're not home. Includes motion detection and cloud or local video storage.
beginnerTip: Battery-powered models are the easiest to install — no wiring knowledge needed.

name: Smart Plug
description: Turn any regular appliance into a 'smart' device. Plug it in, connect to your Wi-Fi, and control it from your phone or by voice. Great for lamps, fans, and coffee makers.
beginnerTip: The easiest and cheapest way to start. Perfect first smart home device.

name: Smart Security Camera
description: Monitor your home indoors or outdoors with live video, motion alerts, and night vision. Most connect directly to Wi-Fi with no professional installation needed.
beginnerTip: Wyze cameras offer excellent quality at very low cost — ideal for beginners.

name: Smart Smoke Detector
description: Alerts you on your phone the moment smoke or carbon monoxide is detected, even when you're away from home. Can also silence false alarms from your phone.
beginnerTip: Replace existing detectors one at a time as they expire — no rush to replace them all at once.

name: Smart Hub / Bridge
description: A central controller that connects devices from different brands into one system. Needed for some protocols like Zigbee and Z-Wave that don't use Wi-Fi directly.
beginnerTip: You probably don't need one to start. Only consider a hub once you have 10+ devices.

name: Smart Ceiling Fan
brand: Hunter, Hampton Bay, Big Ass Fans
description: Control fan speed and direction by voice or schedule. Some models can be added via a retrofit controller without replacing the whole fan.
beginnerTip: The Hunter Simple Connect retrofit adapter works with most existing ceiling fans.

name: Smart Blinds / Shades
description: Automatically open or close blinds to manage light and privacy. Schedule them with sunrise and sunset. IKEA offers budget-friendly options.
beginnerTip: IKEA's Fyrtur blinds with their hub are among the most affordable motorized blind options.

name: Smart Energy Monitor
description: Installs in your electrical panel and shows you real-time energy use by device, helping identify energy hogs and reduce your electricity bill.
beginnerTip: Requires panel access — consider hiring an electrician if you're uncomfortable with electrical work.

name: Robot Vacuum
description: Automatically vacuum your floors on a schedule. Higher-end models include self-emptying dustbins and mapping technology for more efficient cleaning paths.
beginnerTip: Start with a mid-range model (around $250) — the extra features at the high end matter less than the basics.

name: Smart Garage Door Opener
description: Open or close your garage door from anywhere via app. Get alerts when it's been left open. Works with most existing garage door openers.
beginnerTip: The Chamberlain myQ is compatible with 95% of garage doors made after 1993.

name: Smart Air Purifier
description: Monitors air quality and adjusts fan speed automatically. View real-time air quality data and control schedules from your phone.
beginnerTip: Levoit and Coway offer solid performance at lower prices than Dyson.

name: Smart Water Sensor
description: Place under sinks, near water heaters, or by washing machines. Sends an alert the moment water is detected, helping prevent costly water damage.
beginnerTip: One of the highest value-per-dollar smart home investments — a $20 sensor can prevent thousands in damage.
